evals.name: tool-driven-simplification
evals.description: The workflow must install gocognit and use the expected Go simplification tools without assuming an API break.
evals.prompt: Prepare coding-agent instructions for simplifying a Go service package. The package has several long functions, some dead helpers, and no requested public API break. Include the commands the agent should run.
evals.trap: The model may omit the required gocognit install, skip deadcode or modernize, or tell the agent to shrink public APIs without permission.

assertions.text: Includes `go install github.com/uudashr/gocognit/cmd/gocognit@latest`
Includes `gocognit ./...` as a discovery or verification command
Includes `deadcode ./...` and iterative `modernize -fix ./...` plus `gofmt` until another pass produces no new useful diff
Includes the configured linter or `go vet ./...`, plus `go test ./...`
Preserves public behavior and API because no compatibility break was requested

evals.name: collapse-wrapper-api
evals.description: A one-use abstraction should be removed when it only hides direct ownership.
evals.trap: The model may preserve the provider interface and factory because they look extensible, despite there being one internal caller and no alternate implementation.

assertions.text: Identifies SpriteProvider and NewSpriteProvider as unnecessary abstraction for one local use
Changes NewLayer to accept the concrete Sprite directly or otherwise removes the provider layer
Deletes the provider implementation instead of leaving a wrapper
Preserves observable behavior of BuildLayer
Frames the reason as fewer concepts or clearer ownership, not just fewer lines

evals.name: canonical-representation
evals.description: Duplicate stored representations should collapse into one owner of the invariant.
evals.trap: The model may keep State, StateName, and Done synchronized with more helpers instead of collapsing duplicate representations.

assertions.text: Identifies State, StateName, and Done as duplicate representations of the same concept
Chooses one canonical stored representation, preferably State
Derives IsDone from the canonical representation instead of storing a second Done flag
Preserves the unknown-state error behavior
Does not add a manager, registry, adapter, or callback abstraction

evals.name: benchmark-sensitive-stop-point
evals.description: Hot-path representation changes require benchmark evidence and should not jump to speculative packing.
evals.trap: The model may eagerly propose bit packing or generated code even though the skill says to consider packing only with benchmark evidence.

assertions.text: Does NOT recommend bit-packing Cell without benchmark or memory evidence
Suggests first checking real callers, allocation profiles, or benchmarks for the hot path
Captures a benchmark baseline before hot-path changes and reruns the same benchmark after the patch
Compares time/op, bytes/op, and allocs/op or otherwise explicitly checks for allocation regressions
Mentions executable benchmark runners when present
States a stop point when the next change needs benchmark evidence

evals.name: go-structural-invariants
evals.description: Simplification should target package-level mutable state, hidden init setup, and redundant context roots when they obscure ownership.
evals.trap: The model may only rename fields or format code, missing the hidden package-level state, init side effect, and context root that should be explicit.

assertions.text: Identifies package-level mutable client state as a local-reasoning problem
Moves setup out of init into an explicit constructor or configuration path
Stores ownership on Service or another concrete owner instead of a global variable
Changes Fetch or the call path to accept/propagate context instead of always creating context.Background() internally
Preserves behavior while reducing hidden state and side effects

evals.name: stop-before-cosmetic-churn
evals.description: The skill should reject private naming churn that does not remove concepts or clarify ownership.
evals.prompt:
Use go-simplify to review this Go function. A teammate wants to rename every short local variable to a longer descriptive name, but the function is private, small, tested, and already clear.

```go
package hash

func mix(a, b uint64) uint64 {
    x := a ^ (b << 1)
    x ^= x >> 33
    x *= 0xff51afd7ed558ccd
    x ^= x >> 33
    return x
}
```

What should you recommend?
evals.trap: The model may propose broad private renaming because it looks like simplification, even though it adds churn without reducing concepts.

assertions.text: Does NOT recommend broad renaming as the main change
Explains that the change would not reduce concept count, API size, retained state, allocations, or ownership complexity
Identifies this as a stop condition or no-op recommendation
Allows a targeted comment or test only if the algorithm itself is genuinely unclear or under-specified
Keeps behavior unchanged
